general.description: What last night's run found, and how the numbers have moved

empty.disabled: Nightly insights are switched off. Nothing is being measured and nothing is being spent. Switch on Generate insights every night in the plugin settings to start; the first report appears after the next nightly run.
empty.noRuns: No run has finished yet. The task runs once a night, so the first report appears the morning after the feature is switched on.
empty.nothingFound: This run found nothing worth reporting. Its counts still feed the numbers and trends below.
empty.pruned: This run is older than your retention window of {days} days. Its findings quoted shoppers, so they were deleted along with those conversations; its counts and the trends below are kept.

trends.title: Trends
trends.subtitle: The last 30 runs, oldest on the left.
trends.noRuns: There are no runs to plot yet.
trends.searches: Turns where the shopper found nothing, or too much

technical.title: Technical
technical.description: Numbers for whoever maintains the shop: turns that broke off before the assistant could answer, escalations with no destination set, and how often a shortlist was narrow enough for a description excerpt to reach the model.
technical.noRun: No run has finished yet, so there is nothing to count.
technical.escalationHint: Shoppers asked for a person and the assistant had nowhere to send them. Set an escalation destination in the plugin settings.

terms.title: What was searched
terms.caption: The assistant's first search term for each of these turns, built from what the shopper wrote. Not the shopper's own words.
terms.pruned: The words were deleted with the conversations they came from. The count is kept.
terms.capped: The first {count} only; there were more.

empty.advice: Nothing in the catalogue matched. Either the products are missing, or they are described in other words.

overCap.advice: Too many products matched for the assistant to answer. These need narrower filters, not more stock.

metric.judgeConversationsDropped: Conversations left out of the judge
